output.summary: KEP-2727 adds a native gRPC probe type (grpc: port, service) to Pod container Liveness, Readiness and Startup probes, so kubelet can call the standard gRPC health Check method without a packaged helper binary. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Existing workarounds (an extra HTTP health endpoint, or shipping a gRPC client in the image for exec probes) carry overhead and limitations, and gRPC is widely used with load balancers. The KEP proposes kubelet-side gRPC probes using the standard health-checking Check method, with a static kube-probe User-Agent. Reviewers raised TLS and certificate handling, and the feature stayed beta for several releases while adoption was tracked.

alternatives.why_not: The KEP lists it as the alternative and argues that exec probes with a bundled gRPC client have many limitations and overhead.

alternatives.option: Expose an additional HTTP endpoint for health checks
alternatives.why_not: The motivation names it as an existing workaround with limitations and overhead, which native gRPC probes avoid.

alternatives.option: Support the Watch method of the health service
alternatives.why_not: The proposal says Watch is not supported but may be considered in future iterations.

alternatives.option: Use client certificates or verify the server certificate
alternatives.why_not: The proposal says the kubelet probe will not allow client certificates nor verify the server certificate; only unencrypted HTTP/2 and QUIC are excluded for now.

evidence.quote: As spec'd, the `kubelet` probe will not allow use of client certificates nor verify the certificate on the container.
Using `Watch` method of the healthcheck service is not supported, but may be considered in future iterations.
This feature is in beta and enabled by default. Unfortunately there is not much adoption of it yet.
We do insecure connection (equivalent of `-tls-no-verify` in grpc-health-probe), but it will be hard to support certificate-based checks
